conventions.convention: The sphere is outward-oriented in right-handed spatial coordinates. Dot and cross products extend complex-bilinearly; the Hermitian product conjugates its first argument.
Helicity σ ∈ {+1,−1} is the eigenvalue of C_n z = i n × z; P_σ = (P_T + σ C_n)/2 and v_σ = (e_θ + iσ e_φ)/√2.
The real Berry connection is A = i v†dv. Rephasing v′ = exp(iχ)v gives A′ = A − dχ; projected differentiation is locally da − iAa.
Rotations are proper active rotations with the positive sine term n × z. Their helicity character is exp(−iσα), whereas connection holonomy in one frame is exp(i∮A).

Transport allows piecewise C¹ loops with endpoint-continuous one-sided derivatives. The Stokes clause additionally requires smooth-singular path segments and a finite smooth singular spanning chain lying entirely in one open unit-frame domain.
The latitude is traversed with increasing longitude, 0 < θ₀ < π, and its north-cap solid angle is Ω = 2π(1 − cos θ₀).

The construction concerns dimensionless direction-sphere geometry of smooth source-free nonzero classical vacuum Fourier modes; its phases are geometric deductions, without empirical or quantized claims.

load_bearing.statement: L_σ(n) is the range of P_σ(n) = (P_T(n) + σC_n)/2. These fibres form a smooth rank-one complex vector subbundle of S² × C³. A unit frame v defines A = i v†dv and local curvature F = dA.

For σ ∈ {+1,−1}, the spherical frame has A_σ = σ cos θ dφ and F_σ = −σ sin θ dθ ∧ dφ. The curvature extends globally as −σ ω_S², has outward flux −4πσ, and the line bundle has no globally smooth unit frame.

R_n,α acts on L_σ(n) by exp(−iσα). Parallel transport has the stated segment-exponential and transition-factor holonomy; in one frame it is exp(i∮A). For the stipulated smooth singular spanning chain in one frame domain, it equals exp(i∫Σ F_σ).

published_dependencies.used_for: Right-handed coordinate cross product, extended complex-bilinearly in the owned definition.
Euclidean dot product and norm underlying directions, transverse planes, and normalized local sections.
Orientation-ray convention for the outward-oriented direction sphere.
Smooth differential forms used for the connection and curvature.
Pointwise wedge product in the curvature and area-form formulas.
Exterior differentiation of component functions and connection forms.
Gauge invariance of curvature under A′ = A − dχ.
Finite real smooth singular chains, ordered faces, and boundary cancellation for the octahedral sphere cycle.
Pullback integration over ordered affine simplices and finite-chain integration.
Zero integral of a globally exact curvature over the explicit sphere cycle, and the restricted spanning-chain holonomy formula.
